sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Assessment Origin**: The MoES report (2020) is the first comprehensive climate assessment for India, providing a baseline for future policy. 
• **Temperature Trend**: India's average temperature has risen by ~0.7°C during 1901–2018, primarily due to **Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions** and **Land Use Land Cover Change (LULCC)**. 
• **Monsoon Dynamics**: While total monsoon rainfall has decreased, the frequency of **localized heavy rainfall events** has increased, indicating a shift in the hydrological cycle. 
• **Key Metric**: **Radiative Forcing** and **Sea Surface Temperature (SST)** anomalies in the Indian Ocean are the primary drivers of regional climate variability.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Rapid warming, glacier retreat, and permafrost degradation.
Elevation-dependent warming (EDW) and black carbon deposition.
Sea-level rise (SLR) at ~3.3 mm/year; increased cyclonic intensity.
Thermal expansion of oceans and melting of polar ice caps.
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) norms and migration.

items.term: Assessment of Climate Change over the Indian Region (MoES)
items.definition: The authoritative document providing scientific evidence for India's climate policy; it serves as the national equivalent of the IPCC reports.
The 'Indian Niño'; a sea-surface temperature anomaly that significantly modulates the Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall (ISMR).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **NAPCC**: National Action Plan on Climate Change with 8 missions (e.g., National Solar Mission, National Water Mission). 
• **Climate Change Action Plan (CCAP)**: State-level implementation strategies to align with national targets.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Data gaps in regional climate modeling and socio-economic vulnerability mapping. 
• **Solutions**: Strengthening the 'Climate Data Portal' and integrating 'Climate-Resilient Agriculture' (CRA) into district planning.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'H-A-T-S' (Himalayas, Agriculture, Temperature, Sea-level). 
• **Decoded Meaning**: These are the four critical sectors identified by the MoES report as most vulnerable to climate change in India.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Climate Change' (long-term trends) with 'Weather Variability' (short-term events). Always look for the 'multi-decadal' keyword.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Climate Justice' and 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR)' when discussing India's stance in international climate negotiations.

keyTakeaways: India's warming is driven by both global GHG emissions and regional aerosol/land-use changes.
The frequency of extreme weather events is rising faster than the mean change in climate variables.
Institutional response is shifting from mitigation-only to a balanced 'Mitigation + Adaptation' framework.
